extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, researchers, students, and technically-informed general readers)
extracted.subtask_description: A journal-page collection of book reviews, short research/observation letters, and methodological notes that evaluate books and report small scientific findings or experimental suggestions across disciplines. The rubrics address how to judge reference books, textbooks, monographs, short scientific reports, and experimental observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and quality of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the book or article well written and easily readable (e.g., 'Well written', 'The volume is very readable')?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, well-paced prose that makes complex material accessible is a major positive; avoid dense, lifeless, or purely encyclopaedic presentation ('dreary, lifeless, and incomprehensible'). Readability can convert large compilations into useful works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and graphical support
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and adequacy of illustrations, maps, plans, diagrams and sections (e.g., 'profusely illustrated with photographs, maps, plans, diagrams and sections').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good illustration complements concise text and helps cover wide subjects in limited space. Poor or missing figures reduce utility for technical readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and efficient coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a work 'covers a wide subject in a minimum of space' and presents essential material without unnecessary bulk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective condensation that still provides essential concepts and references is praiseworthy. Over-ambitious breadth that sacrifices depth or accuracy is a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of recent literature / up-to-date information
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the author has drawn on recent and relevant literature to keep descriptions current (e.g., 'the author has drawn on most of the more recent literature').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference works should incorporate contemporary findings; omission of recent sources reduces reliability and usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy and editorial precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy of facts, definitions, place-names, and spellings (e.g., 'several minor errors occur in the spelling of place-names', incorrect factual statements in entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference and technical works must minimize typographical and factual errors; such mistakes undermine authority and should be corrected in later editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and quality of bibliography and prefatory material
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality and usefulness of bibliographies and prefatory discussions (e.g., 'bibliography, and a noteworthy preface by M. Louis Mrazec').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good bibliography and insightful preface add significant value by guiding readers to deeper sources and framing the work's approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target-audience alignment (commercial vs scientific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of content and tone for the intended audience (e.g., 'will doubtless make its appeal more to the commercial than to the scientific community').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and editors should tailor scope, level of detail, and emphasis to their intended audience; mismatches (e.g., commercial focus in a work purporting to be scientific) reduce usefulness to primary readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and reliability for reference works
rubrics_metrics.description: Perceived authority, accuracy, and trustworthiness required for works intended as broad references (e.g., 'lacks in many cases that atmosphere of authority and degree of accuracy').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference books aimed at widespread use must maintain rigorous editorial standards and authoritative definitions; loose or erroneous definitions are serious defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision of technical definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Exactness and correctness of definitions of technical/geological/chemical terms (e.g., loose or erroneous definitions like 'zolian' or 'Cambrian' usage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions should be precise and scientifically defensible; overly loose, popularized, or incorrect definitions mislead readers and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionality and balance of coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether topics are allotted space in proportion to their importance (e.g., 'oil potentialities and realities of Great Britain are allotted space out of all proportion').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should ensure that geographic, topical, or thematic emphasis reflects objective importance rather than local or authorial bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate selection and omission of content
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicious inclusion or exclusion of material to maintain usefulness (e.g., suggestion that biographies and some complicated chemical definitions could be dispensed with to include drilling terms intelligible to non-technical readers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For single-volume or concise works, prioritize entries that serve the core user (practical terms, commonly used techniques) and omit peripheral material that reduces space for essential items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical synthesis versus mere compilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which a work synthesizes facts to forecast or analyze rather than serving as a dry compilation of statistics (e.g., Pogue's book uses past and present facts to foreshadow future possibilities rather than being a 'blue-book').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical interpretation, critical judgment, and synthesis increase a work's value compared with bare statistics or lists; avoid producing a dull compendium without insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability and engagement in economic/technical writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoidance of dreary presentation in favour of engaging, skillful handling (e.g., Pogue's book 'demands most careful perusal' and is not dreary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good exposition in economic and technical topics requires lucid structure and argument; dry enumerations should be replaced with explanatory narrative where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate emphasis on neglected but important topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving sufficient space to emerging or important subtopics (e.g., more space to oil-shale and more severe criticism of present refinery practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should anticipate reader needs and devote adequate attention to crucial but under-covered topics; reviewers may recommend expanded treatment in future editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical criticism and rigorous assessment of practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Willingness to critically evaluate contemporary techniques and designs (e.g., 'present refinery practice might with advantage be more severely criticised').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books and reviews should include informed technical critique rather than uncritical descriptions, especially when practice has clear defects or room for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary orientation: scientific vs economic focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity about whether a work is primarily of scientific interest or economic/industrial interest (e.g., geological survey volume is 'scientific rather than an economic interest').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should state their orientation and target readership; conflating or obscuring the primary aim can mislead potential readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of introductory theoretical chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of introductory or theoretical material that frames detailed studies (e.g., 'excellent study of the formation of the faults and fissures and the mode of their filling').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong introductory chapters that synthesize background and theory enhance the value of subsequent descriptive or regional material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical structure and progression (textbooks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical teaching sequence and practical examples for student textbooks (e.g., progression from instruments → plain geometry → solid geometry → details, and recommendation for models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks should follow a clear pedagogical order, introduce necessary tools and concepts before complex topics, and use practical examples and models where beneficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with actual professional practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching and examples should reflect 'proper workmanlike methods of actual engineering practice' rather than school-only hybrid shortcuts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational texts should prepare students for real-world practice by teaching industry-standard methods and avoiding purely academic shortcuts that do not transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of breadth vs depth in compact texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate level of detail for a small/up-to-date book (e.g., 'not overburdened with detail' but 'gives a balanced account').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise books must strike a balance: include sufficient depth to be useful without overloading the reader; include practical methods when theory dominates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of practical laboratory/analytical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of concrete chemical/methodological procedures (e.g., 'inclusion of the chemical methods of separation and analysis' praised).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific texts should include practical procedures and methods alongside theory to be useful to students and practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and presentation of experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity of how experiments are presented (e.g., numbered experiments were 'much less clear and useful than the usual arrangement in tables').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer organization that aids quick reference and comprehension (tables for detection/separation schemes); poorly organized experimental sections reduce usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological completeness: include preliminary tests and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoroughness in experimental/procedural description (e.g., omission of preliminary tests in an acids section is 'a mistake'; plant-tissue inoculation used killed-tissue control).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural descriptions should include standard preliminary tests and appropriate controls; absence of these undermines experimental reliability and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate instrumentation and measurement sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of measurement tools and recommendation to use more sensitive instruments when needed (e.g., used mercury-in-glass thermometers but 'thermo-electric apparatus will naturally be necessary' for further work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select instruments with adequate sensitivity and resolution for the phenomenon; recommend upgrades when preliminary tools lack needed precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental controls for causal inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of control experiments to determine causation (e.g., 'no rise of temperature was observed when the host tissue was killed prior to inoculation'—implying host response role).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate negative/positive controls to distinguish direct pathogen effects from host reactions; report controls explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of analogue laboratory experiments to model larger systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Design of small-scale experiments to mimic larger physical processes (e.g., rotating plate and tank to simulate atmospheric circulation and trades).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed analogue apparatus should capture essential dynamics of the larger system; explicitly state limitations of the analogy and what insight is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting limitations and recommending future work
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors/reviewers should state limitations of the current work and suggest areas for expansion or improvement (e.g., suggest more space for oil-shale, further investigation of upper air winds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly acknowledging limitations and proposing targeted future investigations strengthens scholarly usefulness and guides subsequent research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of nomenclature and standard spellings
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctness of species and technical names (e.g., 'use the correct spelling of two much-discussed names, wigeon and shoveler').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure taxonomic and technical terms are spelled and used correctly; errors can propagate confusion in scientific and popular literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost/accessibility considerations for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Affordability and accessibility of scientific books (e.g., 'gratifying to be able to recommend a volume which is both an inexpensive and necessary addition').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pricing and physical accessibility affect a work's reach and utility; an inexpensive, well-produced volume can be particularly valuable to libraries and students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced presentation of controversial theories
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting controversial or popular theories (e.g., Freudian psychoanalysis) with balance, perspective, and avoidance of uncritical acceptance ('gives a very fair and balanced account', 'keeps these findings in perspective').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writings on contested theories should present evidence, limits, and alternative viewpoints, retaining critical distance and avoiding dogmatic endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and usefulness of classification/frameworks in social-science texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear grouping and diagnostic categories to explain phenomena (e.g., juveniles split into 'mentally too unintelligent' vs 'psychopaths' with differing needs and interventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social-science and policy texts should articulate clear diagnostic or classificatory frameworks that guide interventions; recommendations should follow logically from categories.
